entries.originalText: “My Son, suffer me to do with thee what I will; I know what is expedient for thee.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, allow Me to do with you what I will; I know what is expedient for you.

entries.originalText: Thou thinkest as a man, in many things thou judgest as human affection persuadeth thee.”
entries.modernizedText: You think as a man; in many things you judge as human affection persuades you.”

entries.originalText: Lord, what Thou sayest is true.
entries.modernizedText: Lord, what You say is true.

entries.originalText: Greater is Thy care for me than all the care which I am able to take for myself.
entries.modernizedText: Greater is Your care for me than all the care which I am able to take for myself.

entries.originalText: For too insecurely doth he stand who casteth not all his care upon Thee.
entries.modernizedText: For he stands too insecurely who does not cast all his care upon You.

entries.originalText: Lord, so long as my will standeth right and firm in Thee, do with me what Thou wilt, for whatsoever Thou shalt do with me cannot be aught but good.
entries.modernizedText: Lord, so long as my will stands right and firm in You, do with me what You will, for whatever You do with me cannot be anything but good.

entries.originalText: Blessed be Thou if Thou wilt leave me in darkness: blessed also be Thou if Thou wilt leave me in light.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed are You if You leave me in darkness; blessed also are You if You leave me in light.

entries.originalText: Blessed be Thou if Thou vouchsafe to comfort me, and always blessed be Thou if Thou cause me to be troubled.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed are You if You are pleased to comfort me, and always blessed are You if You cause me to be troubled.

entries.originalText: “My Son! even thus thou must stand if thou desirest to walk with Me.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son! even thus you must stand if you desire to walk with Me.

entries.originalText: Thou must be ready alike for suffering or rejoicing.
entries.modernizedText: You must be ready alike for suffering or rejoicing.

entries.originalText: Thou must be poor and needy as willingly as full and rich.”
entries.modernizedText: You must be poor and needy as willingly as full and rich.”

entries.originalText: Lord, I will willingly bear for Thee whatsoever Thou wilt have to come upon me.
entries.modernizedText: Lord, I will willingly bear for You whatever You will have come upon me.

entries.originalText: Without choice I will receive from Thy hand good and evil, sweet and bitter, joy and sadness, and will give Thee thanks for all things which shall happen unto me.
entries.modernizedText: Without choosing I will receive from Your hand good and evil, sweet and bitter, joy and sadness, and will give You thanks for all things that happen to me.

entries.originalText: Keep me from all sin, and I will not fear death nor hell.
entries.modernizedText: Keep me from all sin, and I will not fear death or hell.

entries.originalText: Only cast me not away for ever, nor blot me out of the book of life.
entries.modernizedText: Only do not cast me away forever, or blot me out of the book of life.

entries.originalText: Then no tribulation which shall come upon me shall do me hurt.
entries.modernizedText: Then no tribulation that comes upon me will do me hurt.
